text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- October consumer price index up 0.8 percent; yearly inflation at 11 percent.
- Hamas activist blows himself up; Israeli army eases closure.
- Hebron talks resume today; Palestinian President Yasser Arafat accuses Israel of delaying agreement.
- Scitex loses $151 million in third quarter and plans to reduce costs in Graphic Arts group significantly.
- Telephone hot line for "closet Jews" set up in Poland.
HAARETZ

- Government adopts programme "to strengthen Israeli sovereignty in East Jerusalem." Among proposals: Opening of a police station and additional government offices, improvement in physical infrastructure and attention to education. Committee headed by Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani.
- Two babies who underwent Conservative conversions in Israel received certification from abroad -- and were listed as Jews.
- Study: Arabs presented in textbooks as "murderers," "rioters," and "robbers".
MAARIV
- Scitex: $151 million loss in quarter; 400 to be sacked.
- Cellcom begins taking steps ahead of entering New York Stock Exchange.
- Hizbollah: Israel failed in bid to liquidate official.
- Terrorist active in Hamas killed preparing bomb.
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai to Sunday Times: In event of war we'll destroy the regime of Syrian President Hafez al-Assad.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Russian scientists help Syria make nerve gas, Mordechai tells Sunday Times.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pressures Mordechai to remove Major-General Oren Shahor from talks with Palestinians.
